Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start the Second innings of the match. The players and the Umpires are at the crease ready to get things underway. It's Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett to open the batting for England. Jasprit Bumrah starts the attack for India. Let's Play!
... SECOND INNINGS ...

England on the other hand should be happy with the way they have bowled and picked up the wickets of the Indian middle order. It would have been worse for England if any of the Indian batters other than Yashasvi Jaiswal had converted their start onto a big score. Both England’s young spinners bowled really well and got the rewards. Rehan Ahmed and Shoaib Bashir on debut, both grabbed 3-3 wickets each and the English veteran James Anderson grabbed 3 for himself. Now, England have the task of batting well on a wicket that still looks good for the batters and is expected to play well throughout the day today. Stay tuned as England comes out to bat soon to start their first innings, chasing 396 posted by India.

With that, we come to the end of the India innings and India has managed to put up a first-innings total of 396 after batting for 112 overs. The Indian batting card shows most of their batters getting decent starts and then throwing away their wickets on a good batting surface on Day 1. India still managed to reach close to the 400 mark all thanks to the brilliant innings by Yashasvi Jaiswal who batted long for his maiden Test Double Century, scoring 209 off 290 balls, which included 19 boundaries and 7 sixes, holding the end from one side and batting through the innings. India now come out to bowl and will look to get early wickets and exert pressure straight away on England.

OUT! TAKEN! Another sharp catch from Joe Root and it is the debutant, Shoaib Bashir who finishes things off! India fall 4 runs short of 400! Comes in from around the wicket and bowls it quicker through the air, angling away, on off, Mukesh Kumar tries to get on the front foot to block it out. He fails to get to the pitch of the ball and pays the price for it. The ball rises off the deck and catches the shoulder of the bat. The ball flies quickly to the right of first slip where Joe Root reacts quickly and takes a good catch at shoulder height. Shoaib Bashir finishes with three wickets and India have been bowled out for 396 in their first innings!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to commence on Day 2! It is a bright and sunny morning in Visakhapatnam as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. They are followed by Ben Stokes and the rest of the England players. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Ravichandran Ashwin are all set to resume their innings for India. England are starting the day with the old ball and it has been handed to the debutant, Shoaib Bashir. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Dinesh Karthik and Eoin Morgan are pitchside. Morgan starts by saying that there are no real signs of deterioration aesthetically. Mention that the odd ball was slowing up on Day 1, and there was variable bounce as well. Feels that day by day, the bounce will continue to be up and down. Adds that there might not be much turn. Reckons that Day 2 and Day 3 are two big days in gaining control of the Test. Karthik ends by saying that it is a very interesting day for both teams.

On the other hand, England will be pleased with how Day 1 turned out for them. Despite losing the toss, James Anderson and the spin quartet were disciplined throughout and did not allow India to run away with the game. With the pitch expected to deteriorate as the Test progresses, England will aim to wrap up the Indian innings quickly, especially with the second new ball due. With not much batting left in the tank, India will be hoping that this pair of Jaiswal and Ashwin can bat for as long as possible. Will England manage to keep India under 400? We shall find out soon, as the first ball is not far away.

India's performance on Day 1 saw them get to 336, although they may rue missed opportunities to capitalise on their starts. Opting to bat first, the Indian openers began cautiously, with Yashasvi Jaiswal demonstrating resilience and building partnerships throughout the day. Despite his teammates falling to make their starts count, Jaiswal's unbeaten innings of 179 propelled the hosts past 300 on a slow-turning surface. As he nears his maiden Test double-century, all eyes will be on his approach at the start of Day 2.

Greetings, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to our coverage of Day 2 of the second Test between India and England at the Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam. It was a captivating day of Test cricket where the momentum swung back and forth, ultimately concluding with England holding a slight advantage at Stumps.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that wraps up the opening day of the second Test where the game ebbed and flowed throughout the 93 overs. With the surface likely to behave the same on Day 2 as it did on Day 1, India will be desperate to bat for as long as they can and the onus will be on Yashasvi Jaiswal again. As for England, the second new ball is due and they are likely to take it straight away on Day 2 in their quest to get into the Indian tail. It promises to be another riveting day of Test cricket. Day 2 will begin on Saturday, 3rd of February at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) but you can join us a lot sooner for the build-up. Cheers!

India's man of the moment, Yashasvi Jaiswal is in for a chat. He talks about his batting, saying that he was looking to bat session by session and was looking to stick to the wicket from one end as there were wickets falling from the other end. He adds that he would love to extend this to a double hundred and take his team to a better position tomorrow. Ends by saying that the wicket has started to do things and is not gonna be the same when India comes in to bat the second time, so the runs that are being scored right now are very important for the course of the Test match.

After choosing to bat first, the Indian openers approached cautiously to assess the pitch. Rohit Sharma fell early, but Jaiswal settled in and received support from Shubman Gill, who departed just before Lunch. Jaiswal continued to excel post-Lunch, reaching his second Test century. However, Shreyas Iyer and Rajat Patidar failed to capitalize on their starts and perished on either side of the Tea interval. Jaiswal then partnered with Axar Patel, who was promoted up the order, but Axar's promising innings was cut short as he was dismissed for 27. Playing on his home ground, KS Bharat got a few boundaries away and looked in great nick until he was dismissed on 17. Jaiswal was unfazed by what was happening at the other end and held his composure to remain unbeaten on 179. He along with Ravichandran Ashwin successfully saw through that tricky phase before the close of play to ensure there were no more hiccups.

Earlier in the day, it was the veteran James Anderson who set the tone as he bowled with immaculate control and did not give much away to the Indian openers. The debutant, Shoaib Bashir was the first to get the breakthrough before Anderson came back to remove Gill before Lunch. In the second session, Joe Root was a bit expensive but Rehan Ahmed, Tom Hartley and Shoaib Bashir combined well to keep India in check with Hartley getting the only wicket to fall in the second session. As the players returned from Tea, Rehan Ahmed got into the act as he got rid of the set Rajat Patidar. Despite being put under pressure by Jaiswal, Bashir came roaring back to remove Axar Patel before Rehan nipped Bharat in the bud towards the end of the day.

SESSION SUMMARY - 111 runs, 30 overs and 3 wickets. End of an absorbing day of Test cricket! Both teams traded blows back and forth but it will be England who will be the happier of the two sides. They kept chipping away with wickets to peg the hosts back at regular intervals throughout the day. As for India, they have gone past 300 but they will be disappointed as it was a story similar to the Hyderabad Test where the batters got off to starts but failed to go on and get the big score for their team. Yashasvi Jaiswal was the stand-out performer for them and he stands unbeaten on 179.

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

England have been bowling well but the wicket is a good one for batting and there is not much help from the wicket to the bowlers. A few balls turning here and there and very few keeping low, including the ball that got Shreyas Iyer out, gives a hint on how the wicket is going to play after a few days and it's going to get tough to bat. Tom Hartley again got the important breakthrough but since then Ben Stokes and the others have been made to think a lot about the current plans applied. England needs to pick up a few wickets in the final session of the game as they don't want to fall behind from the first day of the game itself. As for now, the players and the umpires are enjoying a cup of tea and will come back in 20 minutes to start the third and final session on Day 1 of this Test match.

It's time for a cup of TEA! With that, we come to the end of the second session on Day 1 of this Test match and India look absolutely in control at the moment at 225/3 after 63 overs in the day. With Yashasvi Jaiswal still at the crease on 125, batting brilliantly since the start, along with the debutant Rajat Patidar batting well on 25 stitching up another good partnership after the loss of Shreyas Iyer in this session. India totally winning this session with 122 runs in 32 overs after losing one one wicket.
Bashir gives the ball air and bowls it full, on middle, Rajat Patidar flicks it off his pads but straight to mid-wicket. That will be TEA on DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second session on Day 1! The two umpires make their way out to the middle as do the players of England. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shreyas Iyer are all set to resume their innings for India. It will be Joe Root to start the proceedings with the ball. A slip in place. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

On the other hand, England will be feeling just a bit better after dismissing Shubman Gill just before the Lunch interval. The veteran James Anderson started well with the new ball, as did Joe Root from the other end. Anderson was miserly as ever, beating the bat on several occasions in his first spell of five overs. Having the luxury of three spinners, Ben Stokes rotated them well, and the trio of Joe Root, Tom Hartley, and Shoaib Bashir combined well to keep things quiet. It was the debutant, Bashir, who helped England draw the first blood through his maiden Test wicket of Rohit Sharma. As the Indian batters began to put the pressure back on the spinners, Stokes brought his experienced seamer back into the attack. Anderson answered the call by accounting for Gill and gave his side a much-needed breakthrough. Both camps will be fairly pleased with how the first session panned out and England will look for some early inroads at the start of the second session. Join us back again at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) for the start of the second session.

A good finish to the first session for India in this second Test! They would have liked to lose one wicket less but they will be fairly happy with the runs on the board. After winning a crucial toss, India were off to a sedate start. Yashasvi Jaiswal took Joe Root on in his first over and continued to punish the loose deliveries served to him. The Indian skipper, Rohit Sharma, had a bit of a struggle against James Anderson but was relatively solid against the English spinners. However, Rohit got into his shell and paid the price for being overcautious. Coming in at number 3, Shubman Gill was proactive in his approach as he used his feet to tick along. Just as he was beginning to flourish, a lapse in concentration led to his downfall. Jaiswal brought up his intent-laden fifty just before Lunch, and he, along with Shreyas Iyer, ensured that India went into Lunch with only two wickets down. With the surface not having any visible gremlins and also being on the slower side, Jaiswal will look to convert this start into a big score, and Iyer will look to follow suit once he gets his eye in.

FOUR! That is a brilliant shot by Shreyas Iyer to end the session! James Anderson pitches the ball up on the leg stump line and Shreyas Iyer takes the front foot out and plays an on drive from the middle of the ball, racing past mid on to his left and running away to the long on fence, all along the ground. India end the session at 103/2.

Informs that KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja miss out as does Mohammed Siraj, who has been rested.
